history.dynasty: Gond (Rajgond) dynasty - built by the Gond ruler Madan Singh (also named Madan Shah in some sources).
history.period: CONFLICT (verify): Wikipedia's Madan Mahal page dates the fort to the 14th century AD and says it was built by Raja Madan Singh; wanderlog says constructed around 1116 CE by Gond king Madan Shah; imagewrighter.com says the 11th century by the 37th Gond ruler Madan Singh. The Gond rulers reigned over Jabalpur, Mandla and surrounding regions.
history.summary: CSV NAME FLAG: no standalone 'Rani Durgawati Temple' could be found on the web despite targeted searches - this CSV row has been treated as the Rani Durgavati (Madan Mahal) Fort of Jabalpur, the queen's fort-cum-watchtower. Review needed: either rename the CSV row to 'Rani Durgavati Fort (Madan Mahal)' or confirm whether a separate memorial-shrine is intended. The fort sits atop a ~500 m hill in Jabalpur city, a small compact granite stronghold with a stable, war rooms, a small reservoir and the rulers' pleasure chamber; the Balancing Rock, a geological wonder, lies on the way up. It is named after Madan Shah, son of Rani Durgavati (1524-1564), the Gond warrior queen of the Garha principality who resisted the Mughals and died fighting on 24 June 1564; she used this post as a watchtower and is believed to have spent much time here. Local lore credits her with building many temples and tanks around Jabalpur, and her samadhi/memorial is at Barela (Narrai), ~20 km away en route to Mandla. The Archaeological Survey of India restored the fort in the 20th century. Visitor reviews note a Shiva temple and a dargah inside the complex.

name: Rani Durgavati Fort (Madan Mahal)
town_description: Madan Mahal is a locality of Jabalpur city, Madhya Pradesh, centred on the hill fort of the same name. It has its own railway station (Madan Mahal station) and lies close to the city centre; the hill fort offers panoramic views of Jabalpur.
tradition: Hinduism (fort with Shiva temple); the fort is chiefly a historical monument, not an active temple

travel.airport: Jabalpur (Dumna) Airport is the nearest airport (distance not confirmed - verify).
travel.railway: Nearest railway station is Madan Mahal railway station, per Wikipedia's Madan Mahal page.
travel.road: Within Jabalpur city; the fort is reached by climbing steps to the hilltop. Autos are the usual local option for sightseeing in Jabalpur.
